Plant the Moon: Mars Edition 
Will Indoor or outdoor lighting conditions prevail? 
Third graders quest to find the answers… 
 
Planning: 
We filled out multiple Google forms to decide the process and independent variable of this project. 
Crop choice came down to lettuce or spinach due to the cold weather varieties we had on hand. We 
ultimately chose lettuce because of the shortened growing period at ~35 days which made sense to fit 
within the 8 week grow period. We decided to use differences in lighting as the independent variable. 
Students chose to use different types of light over different watering schedules, and amount of light. 
Students were adamant about having an outdoor crop and indoor crop to vary the lighting from the sun 
to a sun lamp. Students chose this, understanding that we live in MN and the weather was getting 
cooler every day. 
Hypothesis: 
The indoor plants will grow larger and faster than the outdoor plants because the lighting and 
environment indoors is more consistent and controlled than the outdoor environment and lighting. 
Responsibilities: 
Each student applied for up to three jobs they were interested in doing for this project. This is the final 
job board, indicating the job for each student.

Growing Period Indoor: 
Start date: October 10th, 2024 
On planting day, we watered all indoor plants with 1.5 oz of water. We watered regularly between 1-2 
oz. every other day, and by October 22nd, we found that none of the seeds had grown. We replanted all 
indoor plants on the 22nd. 
By November 15th, the tallest indoor plant was the control group, at 1.5” and by November 12th, they 
were all falling down and wilting. We weren’t sure if they were doing this because of the soil, the 
watering on top of the plants, or the lighting being too strong. We decided to poke a “watering hole” in 
the corner of each indoor pot. This is where the water was administered for the remaining days of the 
growth cycle. 
Overall, the indoor plants with earth, humus and regolith were the tallest and grew 3” tall.

Growing Period Outdoor: 
Start date October 10th 2024 
On planting day, we watered all outdoor plants with 1.5 oz of water. We watered regularly between 1-
2oz. every other day, and if it rained, we did not water. On November 18th, it rained so much that the 
plants were “drowning”. We poured off the excess water and continued with the experiment. 
On the final day of the experiment, it was 32 degrees outside, and the rain had frozen on the plants. We 
moved them indoors in order to get final measurements. Outdoor plants with soil containing earth, cow 
manure and regolith grew 1.5” total height. This was the tallest of all outdoor plants.

Growth Cycle Outdoor Photos: 
 
 
 
Final Conclusions: 
Did the experiment support our hypothesis? 
Yes. We found that the indoor plants grew larger and faster indoors using a grow light, and all other 
conditions constant.

What changes or improvements would we consider if we repeated the 
experiment? 
1. We would use only one light instead of two because it seemed that the lighting may have been 
the cause of the sprouts wilting when they got larger than 2” tall. 
2. We would think about reducing the ratio of regolith to earth soil. In this experiment, it seemed 
that 50% regolith was very dense and heavy which was our other thought as to why the sprouts 
wilted when they started to grow tall. 
3. We would keep both sets of plants indoors and not challenge the weather outside. 
4. We would explore more hearty seed varieties that have a higher chance at growth. 
 
What did we learn? 
1. “You can grow lettuce in October.” 
2. “The Mars soil was much harder (denser) than regular soil so the roots would stop when they 
tried to grow through the Regolith.” 
3. “Plants take a long time to grow.” 
4. “I think that we all did really well, and I’m glad the plants were able to sprout.” 
5. “It was frustrating that our plants didn’t grow as large as we expected, but we didn’t give up.” 
6. “The challenge is what made it fun.”
